subject: Medicine
title: Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Stabilization Before Endoscopy
preview: Risk assessment, hemodynamic stabilization and early endoscopic evaluation are the practical core of UGIB care.

sections.title: Recognize urgency
points: Repeated syncope, shock, ongoing hematemesis and altered mentation signal higher risk.
Consider variceal bleeding in the setting of portal hypertension and chronic liver disease.

sections.title: Treat the cause
points: Peptic ulcer bleeding, varices, erosions and Mallory–Weiss tears require different targeted treatment plans.
Resuscitation, appropriate medication and early specialist coordination are complementary to endoscopy.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A near-normal initial hemoglobin does not exclude acute major hemorrhage.
Do not assume every black stool represents an active upper GI bleed without clinical assessment.

quickRevision: Hematemesis and melena may reflect upper GI bleeding; hemodynamic instability takes priority over identifying the precise lesion.
Large-bore access, blood counts, crossmatch and a transfusion strategy require assessment of the patient and comorbidities.
Endoscopy provides diagnosis and frequently treatment after initial stabilization.

quiz.question: What is an immediate priority in severe upper GI bleeding?
quiz.explanation: Airway and circulatory stabilization. Consider variceal bleeding in the setting of portal hypertension and chronic liver disease.
